newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end lower on long-liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end lower on long-liquidation.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo corn futures ended lower across the board on Monday, pressured by long-liquidation, following the lower Chicago market last Friday, traders said.
Prices ranged from 270 yen to 340 yen per tonne lower. Benchmark September was down 310 yen at 14,880 yen. Daily volume was 80,597 lots.

Expectations that the Chicago market will fall further fuelled long-liquidation from the opening. But caution about the market being oversold emerged after benchmark September hit a life-of-contract low during the day, traders said.
Traders said the Tokyo corn futures market may lack clear direction until the USDA report to be released later this week.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.90 per bushel at 0815 GMT, up by 0-1/2 U.S. cents from Friday's close.
The spot November CBOT soybean futures were at $7.27 at 0820 GMT, down by 0-1/4 cent from Friday.
